data.narrative:
Material Evolution is a Series A-stage housing and construction company founded by Liz Gilligan and Sam Clark. The valuation analysis draws on a narrow comp universe of two private peers (Inversion Space and Cobod) with no public comparables available in the sector, limiting external benchmarking precision.

The stage-progression method was the applicable valuation approach. Using the company's $15M in total capital raised as a valuation proxy, a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A progression yields an implied valuation of $30M. This reflects standard dilution and value-creation expectations between early Series A and subsequent funding rounds.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $26M to $34M, with a median point of $30M. The relatively narrow band reflects reliance on a single methodology rather than convergence across multiple approaches. Key uncertainties include the lack of public market comparables in housing and construction technology, limited depth in the private comp set, and typical Series A execution risks around product-market fit and unit economics. Any revised valuation would require additional data on peer funding rounds, revenue multiples, or margin profiles to strengthen conviction.
